lead.title: India's opposition parties march to top court as protests over voter lists escalate
lead.note: Opposition parties in India are marching to the country's top court as protests over changes to the voter roll escalate. They say revisions to the list of eligible voters favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party. Authorities have removed more than 130 million names from the voter roll. The story is a large-scale election dispute with consequences for millions of voters, and it is still developing. Drop Site News also reports that authorities used heavy force against demonstrators in Delhi after the election commission's purge. For a reader following world affairs, the key questions are the legal challenge now before the court and how the election commission responds. The summary available here does not say how the court will rule or what the commission's justification is.
lead.headline: India's Opposition Marches to Top Court Over Voter Lists
decks: Opposition parties say voter list revisions favor Modi's party
